messages.content: I have a new site visit in Central Oregon. Bend treatment facility, gate at 6:30 a.m. Wednesday. They may add a Thursday council debrief. I need a flight, car, and hotel shortlist, not booking yet.

Understood. What Tuesday date, which Bay Area airport should I start with, and how late can you arrive before slide review gets squeezed? Also, are you carrying anything bulky or is the demo skid shipping separately?

Tuesday July 14. Start with SFO but check OAK/SJC only if they are cleaner. I need time to land at Redmond, pick up a car, drive to Bend, and still review slides after dinner. Skid ships separately, but paperwork is not cleared yet.
Got it. I will focus on RDM arrivals Tuesday with enough evening buffer. For routing, is a nonstop worth a modest premium, or should I include one-stop options if they save money?
Nonstop is better if the difference is modest. One short connection is acceptable; I don't want to spend half a day in Seattle or Portland. If Thursday happens, it would probably end around lunch.

Flight shortlist: best fit is United SFO-RDM nonstop Tue 1:05 p.m.-2:42 p.m.; plenty of time for rental pickup, 25-35 minutes to Bend, dinner, and slide review. Acceptable backup is Alaska SFO-SEA-RDM 11:50 a.m.-3:55 p.m. with a 62-minute SEA connection, about $80 less. I would not use OAK/SJC unless price becomes the driver; the routings either connect longer or point you toward Portland plus a long drive.
How tight is that Seattle connection in reality? I don't want to worry about a missed bag even if I am trying not to check one.

Sixty-two minutes in Seattle is workable, but it is not as clean as the nonstop. If you end up checking a case or samples, the nonstop is the better fit. The Alaska option is only the acceptable backup because it saves some money without adding a second stop.
Then keep the nonstop on top. What about return options if the debrief is still pending?

Two ways to protect it: hold a Thursday late-afternoon return, RDM-SFO nonstop around 4:45 p.m., which works if the debrief ends near noon; or keep a Wednesday 6:10 p.m. return as the no-debrief option, but that makes Wednesday a very long day after a 6:30 gate. I would not book the Wednesday return until they confirm the council piece.
Agree. Include the Thursday return as the planning case. Rental car?

RDM airport counters have compact automatic around $52/day, midsize around $61/day, and small SUV around $75/day. For July roads and no bulky gear, compact is fine. I would keep pickup and return at the terminal, no off-airport shuttle.
Compact works. Hotel comparison: one Redmond airport property versus a Bend hotel closer to the plant and dinner.

Redmond logistics option: Hampton Inn Redmond/Bend Airport area, guest rating about 4.5, easiest after landing, free parking, typical in-room coffee/fridge, but a 30-35 minute pre-dawn drive to the Bend facility and fewer dinner choices. Bend work option: Hilton Garden Inn Bend/Old Mill, about 4.4, self-parking, coffee/fridge listed, several restaurants nearby, and roughly 15-20 minutes to the facility. Higher-comfort option: Oxford Hotel Bend, about 4.7, great downtown dining and quieter feel, but materially pricier and less necessary for this trip.
Least painful Wednesday morning?
The Bend option. You can leave around 5:50 and still have margin for the 6:30 gate. From Redmond I would leave closer to 5:25, and any road delay feels more annoying at that hour.
Any catch with the Hilton Garden Inn? Parking, noise, breakfast, and do the rooms actually have a fridge and coffee maker?

No major catch. Parking is straightforward, and breakfast may start too late for the 6:30 gate, so plan on coffee in the room and a grab-and-go item. The room listings show a coffee maker and mini-fridge; I would still add a note requesting both, plus a quiet room away from the main road or elevator.
Oxford sounds nicer but probably overkill. Keep it as a backup. Does the Bend hotel have enough rating cushion, or is this a borderline pick?

It is not borderline. The guest feedback is solid, just not boutique-level. For this trip the trade is sensible: shorter early drive, easier dinner, parking, and room basics. Oxford is the upgrade backup if you decide sleep quality is worth the extra cost.
Summarize the plan and what you need from me before booking.

Best fit to book once cleared: United SFO-RDM nonstop Tue Jul 14 1:05-2:42; compact automatic at the RDM terminal; Hilton Garden Inn Bend/Old Mill Tue-Thu on a refundable rate with quiet-room, coffee, and mini-fridge requests; United RDM-SFO Thu Jul 16 around 4:45 p.m. if the council debrief ends near noon. Acceptable backups: Alaska one-stop via Seattle if price becomes important, Oxford Bend if you want the nicer hotel. Ask before booking: confirm Thursday debrief timing and confirm the demo skid paperwork has cleared. Until then I would not ticket anything nonrefundable.
